# FSS — A Fast Security Scan for developers

> FSS scans Node.js projects for security issues and supply-chain attack
> indicators, cleans `node_modules` safely, and flags outdated dependencies.
> One POSIX shell script, zero runtime dependencies, on macOS and
> Debian-based Linux. MIT licensed, by Coody.

Install:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://fss.coody.app/install.sh | sh
```

The installer places the CLI in `~/.fss` and symlinks it into `~/.local/bin`.
It is short enough to audit before running.

## Commands

- `fss scan [dir]` — seven check groups: lifecycle scripts, known payload
  files, malware code signatures, credential exposure, registry/lockfile
  integrity, rogue binaries, host persistence.
  Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 warnings, 2 critical, 3 error.
- `fss clean [dir] [--dry-run] [--yes]` — lists `node_modules` directories
  with sizes and deletes them after confirmation. Never follows symlinks.
  Exit codes: 0 ok, 3 error.
- `fss outdated [dir]` — compares installed versions against the npm
  registry and highlights major drift. Exit codes: 0 current, 1 outdated,
  3 error.
- `fss update` — self-updates an installed FSS to the latest GitHub release.
  Exit codes: 0 ok, 3 error.

Exit codes are CI-ready: `0` clean, `1` warnings, `2` critical.
